title: Medical-visa planning belongs after clinical fit—not before it
dek: The official e-Visa route has specific categories and documents. A platform should not turn eligibility into a promise.
imageAlt: Illustrative AI-generated planning meeting with no real patient or hospital shown.

sections.heading: What the official portal currently says
paragraphs: India’s official e-Visa portal lists e-Medical and e-Medical Attendant categories. It currently describes a 60-day stay from arrival with multiple entry for the listed e-Medical category, an application window beginning at least four days before arrival, and up to two e-Medical Attendant visas against one e-Medical visa.
Rules depend on nationality, passport, treatment route and current government policy. Always re-check the official portal; a coordinator or hospital letter does not guarantee approval.

sections.heading: A safer order of operations
paragraphs: First confirm that a named receiving team has reviewed enough sourced information to say an in-person assessment may be appropriate. Then obtain the facility’s required invitation or letter, verify passport and category rules, plan a companion where needed, and keep flexible travel arrangements until formal decisions exist.
bullets: Do not buy non-refundable travel based only on a directory profile.
Keep originals and translated copies attributable to their source.
Plan medication continuity, accessibility, recovery accommodation and the return handback.
Use government channels; beware of anyone charging an unofficial ‘emergency visa’ fee.
